predictions.account: Forward causal_return_path_hypothesis: base heating increases tray evaporation, vapor reaches the cooler lid, condensation worsens visibility, and the operator continues or increases heating in response. Every link beyond the supplied temperature, humidity and image observations remains a hypothesis; fixed-power traces do not demonstrate an obscuration-responsive control loop.
predictions.result: If continued heating feeds late vapor supply, cutting the proposed return link from worsening visibility to continued heating should reduce late humidity growth and late obscuration relative to continued 6 W, provided the lid temperatures remain comparable. Record even a partial reduction with its duration and sample temperature. Failure to reach 90% readability is failure of the full target. Cooling after power removal and unmeasured humidity distribution could produce another explanation, so this contrast alone would not establish evaporation or condensation flux.

predictions.account: Reversed causal arrow: obscuration driven by lid temperature, moisture or airflow induces the operator to retain heating, so the association between heating and late fog can partly reflect fog causing heating decisions. This rival concerns the direction of the decision link and can coexist with a physical heating effect.
predictions.result: Under this hypothesis, late obscuration should precede any obscuration-responsive command to retain or raise power; merely seeing 6 W during fog does not prove that command caused it. An imposed power change made before late rebound provides a direction test: a subsequent reproducible humidity or visibility change would support a heating contribution, while fog that develops first under unchanged commands supports an independent initiating cause. Neither ordering alone excludes shared temperature or moisture causes. The supplied fixed-6 W records contain no observed command-response sequence and cannot decide the reversed arrow.

The higher-fan anomaly does not identify which transport or thermal mechanism operated.
predictions.result: If this account dominates, the timed 0 W or 3 W conditions may retain high obscuration or fog earlier despite lower sample temperatures; a change in lid temperature could explain that result without establishing continuous 6 W necessity. If fan routing matters, redirecting the duct away from a direct tray-to-lid route at fixed 6 W and 60% fan may reduce late fog without a large center-air temperature change. That result would support a routing-sensitive effect, but would not directly measure vapor transport or prove a feedback loop.
